addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

KasirKu is being developed as a SaaS-style product to be sold to other business owners (pelaku usaha) — it is not for the developer's (Melan's) own personal store. Confirmed 2026-07-08: Melan has never created an owner account in the app himself; his role is building/selling the system, not operating a store with it.

**Why:** changes the frame for future work — onboarding/signup flow, pricing/subscription, multi-tenant admin oversight, and marketing/landing pages matter here in a way they wouldn't for a single-owner internal tool.

**How to apply:** when working on auth, onboarding, or the root "/" experience, consider that the audience is prospective *customers* signing up for the first time, not one known owner. Currently there is no public marketing/landing page — `/` (`src/app/page.tsx`) just redirects straight to `/dashboard` (which the proxy then redirects to `/login` if unauthenticated). There is also no billing/subscription, plan limits, or super-admin panel for the seller to oversee all tenant businesses — flag these as likely-needed features rather than assuming out of scope. See [[test-account-preview]] for the throwaway test account used for browser verification (that account is not Melan's real account and is unrelated to any future customer-facing signup flow).

name: supabase-migrations-manual
description: Supabase CLI is not linked on this machine — migrations must be applied manually via the dashboard SQL Editor
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 50995607-d66f-437b-ab1d-8d3f149bdbb6
---

The KasirKu project uses a hosted Supabase project (URL in `.env.local`), but `npx supabase migration list --linked` fails with LegacyProjectNotLinkedError — the CLI is not linked on this machine.

**Why:** New files in `supabase/migrations/` do not reach the database automatically; features silently fall back (e.g. missing RPCs return null) until applied.

**How to apply:** After adding a migration, remind the user (m.khamdannn91@gmail.com) to paste its SQL into the Supabase dashboard SQL Editor. As of 2026-07-03 all migrations through `20260702101100_self_order_rpc.sql` are applied (user ran the self-order RPC one manually that day; full customer QR → POS inbox flow verified E2E). `20260703100000_void_transaction_rpc.sql` was applied by the user the same day (void flow verified E2E: PIN gating, stock restore, activity log). `20260703110000_discounts_tax_checkout.sql` was applied by the user the same day (discount/PPN/service checkout verified E2E incl. CSV export columns). `20260703120000_open_bills.sql` was applied by the user the same day (save/update/load/pay-deletes cycle verified E2E). All migrations through 20260703120000 are applied. To verify whether an RPC exists, POST to `/rest/v1/rpc/<fn>` with correct param names; PGRST202 with an empty body is a false negative.

**Why:** changes the frame for future work — onboarding/signup flow, pricing/subscription, multi-tenant admin oversight, and marketing/landing pages matter here in a way they wouldn't for a single-owner internal tool.

**How to apply:** when working on auth, onboarding, or the root "/" experience, consider that the audience is prospective *customers* signing up for the first time, not one known owner. Currently there is no public marketing/landing page — `/` (`src/app/page.tsx`) just redirects straight to `/dashboard` (which the proxy then redirects to `/login` if unauthenticated). 5	
6	Route Groups are a folder convention that let you organize routes by category or team.
7	
8	## Convention
9	
10	A route group can be created by wrapping a folder's name in parenthesis: `(folderName)`.
11	
12	This convention indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.
13	
14	<Image
15	  alt="An example folder structure using route groups"
16	  srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png"
17	  srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-route-groups.png"
18	  width="1600"

23	
24	- Organizing routes by team, concern, or feature.
25	- Defining multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout).
26	- Opting specific route segments into sharing a layout, while keeping others out.
27	
28	## Caveats
29	
30	- **Full page load**: If you navigate between routes that use different root layouts, it'll trigger a full page reload. For example, navigating from `/cart` that uses `app/(shop)/layout.js` to `/blog` that uses `app/(marketing)/layout.js`. This **only** applies to multiple root layouts.
31	- **Conflicting paths**: Routes in different groups should not resolve to the same URL path. For example, `(marketing)/about/page.js` and `(shop)/about/page.js` would both resolve to `/about` and cause an error.

---
title: Route Groups
description: Route Groups can be used to partition your Next.js application into different sections.
---

Route Groups are a folder convention that let you organize routes by category or team.

## Convention

A route group can be created by wrapping a folder's name in parenthesis: `(folderName)`.

This convention indicates the folder is for organizational purposes and should **not be included** in the route's URL path.

<Image
  alt="An example folder structure using route groups"
  srcLight="/docs/light/project-organization-route-groups.png"
  srcDark="/docs/dark/project-organization-route-groups.png"
  width="1600"
  height="849"
/>

## Use cases

- Organizing routes by team, concern, or feature.
- Defining multiple [root layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#root-layout).
- Opting specific route segments into sharing a layout, while keeping others out.

## Caveats

- **Full page load**: If you navigate between routes that use different root layouts, it'll trigger a full page reload. For example, navigating from `/cart` that uses `app/(shop)/layout.js` to `/blog` that uses `app/(marketing)/layout.js`. This **only** applies to multiple root layouts.
- **Conflicting paths**: Routes in different groups should not resolve to the same URL path. For example, `(marketing)/about/page.js` and `(shop)/about/page.js` would both resolve to `/about` and cause an error.
- **Top-level root layout**: If you use multiple root layouts without a top-level `layout.js` file, make sure your home route (/) is defined within one of the route groups, e.g. app/(marketing)/page.js.

name: supabase-migrations-manual
description: Supabase CLI is not linked on this machine — migrations must be applied manually via the dashboard SQL Editor
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 50995607-d66f-437b-ab1d-8d3f149bdbb6
---

The KasirKu project uses a hosted Supabase project (URL in `.env.local`), but `npx supabase migration list --linked` fails with LegacyProjectNotLinkedError — the CLI is not linked on this machine.

**Why:** New files in `supabase/migrations/` do not reach the database automatically; features silently fall back (e.g. missing RPCs return null) until applied.

**How to apply:** After adding a migration, remind the user (m.khamdannn91@gmail.com) to paste its SQL into the Supabase dashboard SQL Editor. As of 2026-07-03 all migrations through `20260702101100_self_order_rpc.sql` are applied (user ran the self-order RPC one manually that day; full customer QR → POS inbox flow verified E2E). `20260703100000_void_transaction_rpc.sql` was applied by the user the same day (void flow verified E2E: PIN gating, stock restore, activity log). `20260703110000_discounts_tax_checkout.sql` was applied by the user the same day (discount/PPN/service checkout verified E2E incl. CSV export columns). `20260703120000_open_bills.sql` was applied by the user the same day (save/update/load/pay-deletes cycle verified E2E). All migrations through 20260703120000 are applied. To verify whether an RPC exists, POST to `/rest/v1/rpc/<fn>` with correct param names; PGRST202 with an empty body is a false negative.

`20260704100000_stock_adjustments.sql` (adds `stock_adjustments` table for the stok opname/adjustment feature) was applied by the user on 2026-07-04. All migrations through 20260704100000 are applied.

`20260704200000_customers.sql` (adds `customers` table, `transactions.customer_id`, and redefines `checkout_transaction` with an 8th optional `p_customer_id` param) was applied by the user on 2026-07-04. All migrations through 20260704200000 are applied.

`20260704300000_low_stock_threshold.sql` (adds `min_stock` to `products` and `ingredients` for the low-stock notification feature) was applied by the user on 2026-07-04. All migrations through 20260704300000 are applied.

`20260705100000_cashier_management.sql` (adds `reset_cashier_pin` RPC) was applied by the user on 2026-07-05. All migrations through 20260705100000 are applied.

As of 2026-07-08, migrations `20260706100000_payroll.sql` through `20260707100000_ticket_checkin.sql` status is unconfirmed (not verified this session). `20260708100000_link_self_order_checkout.sql` (redefines `checkout_transaction` with a 9th `p_self_order_ids uuid[]` param that marks self_orders 'selesai' and stamps `transactions.table_id` on checkout) was applied by the user on 2026-07-08 and verified E2E in browser preview: QR order → POS inbox "+ Ke Kasir" → checkout → self_order auto-flips to 'selesai' and disappears from the inbox with no manual "✓ Selesai" click needed. All migrations through 20260708100000 are applied.

`20260708200000_admin_panel.sql` (adds `public.admins` table + `private.is_admin()` + security-definer RPCs `admin_stats()`/`admin_list_businesses()` for the new read-only `/admin` superadmin panel, see [[project-purpose-saas-product]]) **applied and verified 2026-07-09**. Melan signed up his first real owner account (m.khamdannn91@gmail.com, uid `3b8dcecf-db11-4aa1-b1cb-9ae3e4197c95`) via `/signup` — his first-ever account in the app, per [[project-purpose-saas-product]] — then was seeded into `public.admins` via the dashboard SQL Editor. `/admin` confirmed working in browser preview: shows stats (4 toko, 3 pemilik, F&B/Retail/Tiket breakdown) and full tenant list.

Three more migrations for the new accounting/mini-ERP module (see [[mini-erp-scope]]):
- `20260708300000_accounting_core.sql` — `accounts`, `journal_entries`, `journal_lines` tables, default COA seeded per business (trigger + backfill), `private.post_journal()` helper, `public.post_journal_entry()` manual-entry RPC. **Confirmed applied 2026-07-08**: Daftar Akun page shows all 15 seeded accounts for Toko Test Laporan, and a manual journal entry via the Jurnal page posted successfully and balanced.
- `20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql` — redefines `checkout_transaction` (same 9-param signature, now also auto-posts a sales journal entry) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). **Confirmed applied and working 2026-07-08**: did a real POS sale (Roti Bakar, INV-20260708-0003, Rp19.058) and it auto-posted "Penjualan INV-20260708-0003" — debit Kas & Bank / credit Pendapatan Penjualan Rp19.058, no HPP lines since Roti Bakar has no recipe cost yet (expected). Neraca then showed Total Aset = Total Modal (Laba Berjalan) = Rp19.058, balanced.
- `20260708300200_budgets.sql` — `public.budgets` table for the Target vs Aktual report. Applied alongside 300100 per the user; not separately exercised yet (no budget has been set through the UI) but the table existing is implied by the successful accounting_core + checkout migrations going in without error.

Void auto-reversal **confirmed working 2026-07-08**: voided INV-20260708-0003 (manager PIN 9999 / Manajer Test) and a "Void INV-20260708-0003" journal entry posted automatically with debit/credit swapped from the original sale (debit Pendapatan Penjualan / credit Kas & Bank, Rp19.058) — Neraca's Kas & Bank correctly went back to Rp0 afterward.

Still unverified: expense (`finance` addExpense) auto-posting, and the Anggaran/budgets UI actually saving+reading a target.

Neraca updated and stayed balanced (Total Aset = Total Modal = -Rp50.000, "✓ Aset = Kewajiban + Modal (seimbang)"). Still unverified: the Anggaran/budgets UI actually saving+reading a target.

The KasirKu project uses a hosted Supabase project (URL in `.env.local`), but `npx supabase migration list --linked` fails with LegacyProjectNotLinkedError — the CLI is not linked on this machine.

**Why:** New files in `supabase/migrations/` do not reach the database automatically; features silently fall back (e.g. missing RPCs return null) until applied.

**How to apply:** After adding a migration, remind the user (m.khamdannn91@gmail.com) to paste its SQL into the Supabase dashboard SQL Editor. As of 2026-07-03 all migrations through `20260702101100_self_order_rpc.sql` are applied (user ran the self-order RPC one manually that day; full customer QR → POS inbox flow verified E2E). `20260703100000_void_transaction_rpc.sql` was applied by the user the same day (void flow verified E2E: PIN gating, stock restore, activity log). `20260703110000_discounts_tax_checkout.sql` was applied by the user the same day (discount/PPN/service checkout verified E2E incl. CSV export columns). `20260703120000_open_bills.sql` was applied by the user the same day (save/update/load/pay-deletes cycle verified E2E). All migrations through 20260703120000 are applied. To verify whether an RPC exists, POST to `/rest/v1/rpc/<fn>` with correct param names; PGRST202 with an empty body is a false negative.

`20260704100000_stock_adjustments.sql` (adds `stock_adjustments` table for the stok opname/adjustment feature) was applied by the user on 2026-07-04. All migrations through 20260704100000 are applied.

`20260704200000_customers.sql` (adds `customers` table, `transactions.customer_id`, and redefines `checkout_transaction` with an 8th optional `p_customer_id` param) was applied by the user on 2026-07-04. All migrations through 20260704200000 are applied.

`20260704300000_low_stock_threshold.sql` (adds `min_stock` to `products` and `ingredients` for the low-stock notification feature) was applied by the user on 2026-07-04. All migrations through 20260704300000 are applied.

`20260705100000_cashier_management.sql` (adds `reset_cashier_pin` RPC) was applied by the user on 2026-07-05. All migrations through 20260705100000 are applied.

As of 2026-07-08, migrations `20260706100000_payroll.sql` through `20260707100000_ticket_checkin.sql` status is unconfirmed (not verified this session). `20260708100000_link_self_order_checkout.sql` (redefines `checkout_transaction` with a 9th `p_self_order_ids uuid[]` param that marks self_orders 'selesai' and stamps `transactions.table_id` on checkout) was applied by the user on 2026-07-08 and verified E2E in browser preview: QR order → POS inbox "+ Ke Kasir" → checkout → self_order auto-flips to 'selesai' and disappears from the inbox with no manual "✓ Selesai" click needed. All migrations through 20260708100000 are applied.

`20260708200000_admin_panel.sql` (adds `public.admins` table + `private.is_admin()` + security-definer RPCs `admin_stats()`/`admin_list_businesses()` for the new read-only `/admin` superadmin panel, see [[project-purpose-saas-product]]) **applied and verified 2026-07-09**. Melan signed up his first real owner account (m.khamdannn91@gmail.com, uid `3b8dcecf-db11-4aa1-b1cb-9ae3e4197c95`) via `/signup` — his first-ever account in the app, per [[project-purpose-saas-product]] — then was seeded into `public.admins` via the dashboard SQL Editor. `/admin` confirmed working in browser preview: shows stats (4 toko, 3 pemilik, F&B/Retail/Tiket breakdown) and full tenant list.

Three more migrations for the new accounting/mini-ERP module (see [[mini-erp-scope]]):
- `20260708300000_accounting_core.sql` — `accounts`, `journal_entries`, `journal_lines` tables, default COA seeded per business (trigger + backfill), `private.post_journal()` helper, `public.post_journal_entry()` manual-entry RPC. **Confirmed applied 2026-07-08**: Daftar Akun page shows all 15 seeded accounts for Toko Test Laporan, and a manual journal entry via the Jurnal page posted successfully and balanced.
- `20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql` — redefines `checkout_transaction` (same 9-param signature, now also auto-posts a sales journal entry) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). **Confirmed applied and working 2026-07-08**: did a real POS sale (Roti Bakar, INV-20260708-0003, Rp19.058) and it auto-posted "Penjualan INV-20260708-0003" — debit Kas & Bank / credit Pendapatan Penjualan Rp19.058, no HPP lines since Roti Bakar has no recipe cost yet (expected). Neraca then showed Total Aset = Total Modal (Laba Berjalan) = Rp19.058, balanced.
- `20260708300200_budgets.sql` — `public.budgets` table for the Target vs Aktual report. Applied alongside 300100 per the user; not separately exercised yet (no budget has been set through the UI) but the table existing is implied by the successful accounting_core + checkout migrations going in without error.

Void auto-reversal **confirmed working 2026-07-08**: voided INV-20260708-0003 (manager PIN 9999 / Manajer Test) and a "Void INV-20260708-0003" journal entry posted automatically with debit/credit swapped from the original sale (debit Pendapatan Penjualan / credit Kas & Bank, Rp19.058) — Neraca's Kas & Bank correctly went back to Rp0 afterward.

User wants KasirKu to grow toward a "mini ERP" (2026-07-08), modeled loosely on a reference prototype (`Koenang Resto` — a separate accounting + cost-control app, file at `D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\index.html`, an iframe shell only — actual module content in `modules/akuntansi.html`/`modules/costcontrol.html` was never shared). Explicit instruction: doesn't need to be complete, and must not disrupt the existing system — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

**Why:** the reference's sidebar reveals the target feature set even without the module internals: Akuntansi (COA/Jurnal/Neraca/Arus Kas/Target vs Aktual), Cost Control & HPP (kalkulator HPP, database bahan, cost control, laporan COGS, tren harga), Operasional (pembelian, stok, penjualan, invoice, kas harian, rekon rekening, supplier/hutang), SDM (absensi, payroll, lembur, THR, karyawan).

**Gap analysis against KasirKu's actual code (verified by reading source, not assumed):**
- Already covered, no rebuild needed: Laba Rugi (cash-basis, `reports/laba-rugi`), Payroll+Absensi, Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku, Riwayat Transaksi, Kelola Kasir.
- **Hitung HPP** — already exists: `products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` → `recalculateProductCost()` auto-recomputes `products.cost` from `product_recipes × ingredients.unit_cost` on every add/remove.
- **Cost Control (teori vs aktual)** — already exists in full inside `finance/page.tsx` (~line 187-256): COGS Teori (recipe-based) vs COGS Aktual (opening + pembelian − closing inventory), with a variance box and qualitative waste/efficiency notes. Not obvious from the nav alone — read the file before assuming this is missing.
- **Laporan COGS (per-produk/kategori breakdown)** — was genuinely missing; **built 2026-07-08** at `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, linked from the sidebar ("📐 Laporan COGS" in dashboard-shell.tsx) and cross-linked from `finance/page.tsx`'s Kontrol HPP section. Shows revenue/COGS/margin per category and per product, flags products with no HPP data (cost=0) and products under 20% margin.
- **Tren Harga bahan baku** — still missing, needs a new price-history table (`ingredients.unit_cost` only stores the current value, no history). Not started.
- Full double-entry **Akuntansi module** (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Target vs Aktual) — still entirely missing, and is a much bigger lift (new schema for accounts + journal lines, plus a decision on how it relates to the existing cash-basis Laba Rugi/Keuangan pages — replace or coexist?). Not started; user chose to do Cost Control/HPP first, accounting module "menyusul" (comes after).
- **Operasional gaps** not yet addressed: formal Pembelian (purchasing) records beyond the existing `expenses` category tagging, Supplier & Hutang (accounts payable) tracking — no supplier table exists yet.

**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. When resuming this work, next candidates in rough priority order: Tren Harga (small, additive), Supplier & Hutang / formal Pembelian.

**Akuntansi module — built 2026-07-08** (user explicitly chose auto-posting from transactions, and all 4 reports at once, overriding the "doesn't need to be complete" framing for this specific piece):
- Schema: `public.accounts` (Chart of Accounts, seeded per-business via trigger + backfill with a standard Indonesian F&B/retail COA — Kas & Bank, Persediaan, Utang Dagang, Modal Pemilik, Pendapatan Penjualan, Beban Pokok Penjualan, Beban Gaji/Sewa/Listrik/Marketing/Perlengkapan/Lain-lain), `public.journal_entries` + `public.journal_lines` (double-entry, journal tables are SELECT-only from the client — all writes go through `private.post_journal()` so an unbalanced entry can never be persisted), `public.budgets` (Target vs Aktual). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for the 3 pending migration files.
- Auto-posting wired into `checkout_transaction` (sales → debit Kas/Bank + credit Pendapatan, plus debit HPP/credit Persediaan when the sale has recipe cost data) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). Expense recording (`finance/actions.ts` → `addExpense`) also auto-posts via the new `post_journal_entry` RPC — purchases hit Persediaan, other categories map to a fixed category→account table (`EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT` in that file).
- Payroll does NOT auto-post yet — payslip actions still write directly to tables with no RPC, deliberately deferred rather than expanding this delivery further. If asked to close this gap, same pattern as the expense hook applies.
- 5 new pages under `/business/<id>/accounting/`: `daftar-akun` (CRUD custom accounts, system accounts can't be deleted), `jurnal` (period-filtered list + manual multi-line entry form with live debit=credit balance check), `neraca` (balance sheet as-of a date, with an unclosed "Laba Berjalan" line in Modal since there's no formal period-closing process — if aset≠kewajiban+modal it flags a visible warning), `arus-kas` (cash flow from the Kas & Bank account only, bucketed into Operasional vs "Investasi & Pendanaan (manual)"), `anggaran` (monthly budget per pendapatan/beban account vs actual from the journal). All wired into a new "Akuntansi" sidebar group in `dashboard-shell.tsx` (hidden for `tiket` business type, same as the existing Keuangan/Laporan group).
- Verified pre-migration: all 5 pages render gracefully with empty/zero state (no crashes) since none of them gate on the new tables existing — only real financial correctness (auto-posting, balance changes) remains to verify once the migrations are applied.

---
name: mini-erp-scope
description: "Mini-ERP feature gap analysis against the \"Koenang Resto\" reference HTML the user shared, and what's been built so far"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8e69bf51-0851-4034-a940-3ce164e88520
---

User wants KasirKu to grow toward a "mini ERP" (2026-07-08), modeled loosely on a reference prototype (`Koenang Resto` — a separate accounting + cost-control app, file at `D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\index.html`, an iframe shell only — actual module content in `modules/akuntansi.html`/`modules/costcontrol.html` was never shared). Explicit instruction: doesn't need to be complete, and must not disrupt the existing system — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

**Why:** the reference's sidebar reveals the target feature set even without the module internals: Akuntansi (COA/Jurnal/Neraca/Arus Kas/Target vs Aktual), Cost Control & HPP (kalkulator HPP, database bahan, cost control, laporan COGS, tren harga), Operasional (pembelian, stok, penjualan, invoice, kas harian, rekon rekening, supplier/hutang), SDM (absensi, payroll, lembur, THR, karyawan).

**Gap analysis against KasirKu's actual code (verified by reading source, not assumed):**
- Already covered, no rebuild needed: Laba Rugi (cash-basis, `reports/laba-rugi`), Payroll+Absensi, Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku, Riwayat Transaksi, Kelola Kasir.
- **Hitung HPP** — already exists: `products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` → `recalculateProductCost()` auto-recomputes `products.cost` from `product_recipes × ingredients.unit_cost` on every add/remove.
- **Cost Control (teori vs aktual)** — already exists in full inside `finance/page.tsx` (~line 187-256): COGS Teori (recipe-based) vs COGS Aktual (opening + pembelian − closing inventory), with a variance box and qualitative waste/efficiency notes. Not obvious from the nav alone — read the file before assuming this is missing.
- **Laporan COGS (per-produk/kategori breakdown)** — was genuinely missing; **built 2026-07-08** at `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, linked from the sidebar ("📐 Laporan COGS" in dashboard-shell.tsx) and cross-linked from `finance/page.tsx`'s Kontrol HPP section. Shows revenue/COGS/margin per category and per product, flags products with no HPP data (cost=0) and products under 20% margin.
- **Tren Harga bahan baku** — still missing, needs a new price-history table (`ingredients.unit_cost` only stores the current value, no history). Not started.
- Full double-entry **Akuntansi module** (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Target vs Aktual) — still entirely missing, and is a much bigger lift (new schema for accounts + journal lines, plus a decision on how it relates to the existing cash-basis Laba Rugi/Keuangan pages — replace or coexist?). Not started; user chose to do Cost Control/HPP first, accounting module "menyusul" (comes after).
- **Operasional gaps** not yet addressed: formal Pembelian (purchasing) records beyond the existing `expenses` category tagging, Supplier & Hutang (accounts payable) tracking — no supplier table exists yet.

**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. When resuming this work, next candidates in rough priority order: Tren Harga (small, additive), Supplier & Hutang / formal Pembelian.

**Akuntansi module — built 2026-07-08** (user explicitly chose auto-posting from transactions, and all 4 reports at once, overriding the "doesn't need to be complete" framing for this specific piece):
- Schema: `public.accounts` (Chart of Accounts, seeded per-business via trigger + backfill with a standard Indonesian F&B/retail COA — Kas & Bank, Persediaan, Utang Dagang, Modal Pemilik, Pendapatan Penjualan, Beban Pokok Penjualan, Beban Gaji/Sewa/Listrik/Marketing/Perlengkapan/Lain-lain), `public.journal_entries` + `public.journal_lines` (double-entry, journal tables are SELECT-only from the client — all writes go through `private.post_journal()` so an unbalanced entry can never be persisted), `public.budgets` (Target vs Aktual). See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for the 3 pending migration files.
- Auto-posting wired into `checkout_transaction` (sales → debit Kas/Bank + credit Pendapatan, plus debit HPP/credit Persediaan when the sale has recipe cost data) and `void_transaction` (posts a reversing entry). Expense recording (`finance/actions.ts` → `addExpense`) also auto-posts via the new `post_journal_entry` RPC — purchases hit Persediaan, other categories map to a fixed category→account table (`EXPENSE_CATEGORY_ACCOUNT` in that file).
- Payroll does NOT auto-post yet — payslip actions still write directly to tables with no RPC, deliberately deferred rather than expanding this delivery further. If asked to close this gap, same pattern as the expense hook applies.
- 5 new pages under `/business/<id>/accounting/`: `daftar-akun` (CRUD custom accounts, system accounts can't be deleted), `jurnal` (period-filtered list + manual multi-line entry form with live debit=credit balance check), `neraca` (balance sheet as-of a date, with an unclosed "Laba Berjalan" line in Modal since there's no formal period-closing process — if aset≠kewajiban+modal it flags a visible warning), `arus-kas` (cash flow from the Kas & Bank account only, bucketed into Operasional vs "Investasi & Pendanaan (manual)"), `anggaran` (monthly budget per pendapatan/beban account vs actual from the journal). All wired into a new "Akuntansi" sidebar group in `dashboard-shell.tsx` (hidden for `tiket` business type, same as the existing Keuangan/Laporan group).
- Verified pre-migration: all 5 pages render gracefully with empty/zero state (no crashes) since none of them gate on the new tables existing — only real financial correctness (auto-posting, balance changes) remains to verify once the migrations are applied.
- **Full E2E verification completed 2026-07-09** (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]] for details): expense auto-posting (Lain-lain → debit Beban Lain-lain/credit Kas & Bank, Neraca stays balanced) and the Anggaran/budgets UI (set target, Aktual pulled correctly from journal, variance/% computed correctly) both confirmed working. The whole accounting module (COA, Jurnal, Neraca, Arus Kas, Anggaran) is now fully exercised end-to-end, not just pre-migration render checks. Also seeded a superadmin panel (`/admin`) with Melan's first-ever real account — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. As of 2026-07-09 every item originally identified in this gap analysis has been built and verified E2E — no queued next candidate remains; ask the user what's next if resuming this thread.

**Supplier & Hutang (formal Pembelian) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: migration `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) adds `public.suppliers` (name/phone/address/notes, soft-delete), `public.purchases` (supplier_id nullable, category constrained to `'Bahan Baku'|'Barang Dagang'`, optional ingredient_id/product_id + qty, amount, paid_amount with a `paid_amount <= amount` check), and `public.purchase_payments` (installment log). Deliberately additive/separate from the existing `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` "Pembelian Bahan Baku/Barang Dagang" categories — this is a new, more structured flow for supplier-attributed purchases that can be paid partially or fully on credit, not a replacement.
- New pages: `suppliers/page.tsx` (CRUD list + outstanding-utang badge computed from purchases) and `purchases/page.tsx` (record a purchase — mirrors `add-expense-form.tsx`'s ingredient/product conditional UI and weighted-average cost recalc exactly, plus a 3-way payment-mode picker: Lunas Sekarang / Bayar Sebagian / Semua Utang — with inline "+ Bayar" installment forms per unpaid purchase row).
- `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase` posts a journal entry via the same `post_journal_entry` RPC pattern as `finance/actions.ts` (debit 1-200 Persediaan for the full amount; credit 1-001 Kas & Bank for whatever's paid now, credit 2-001 Utang Dagang for the remainder — 2 or 3 lines depending on payment mode). `addPurchasePayment` posts debit 2-001 / credit 1-001 for each installment and rejects overpayment past the remaining balance. Ingredient purchases also insert into `ingredient_price_history` (source `'pembelian'`) same as the expense flow, see [[mini-erp-scope]]'s Tren Harga section above.
- Nav: "🧾 Pembelian & Hutang" and "🏬 Supplier" added to the Operasional sidebar group (not fnb-gated — retail businesses get both too, just without the ingredient option; tiket excluded like the rest of Operasional's inventory items).
- Verified in browser: added supplier "CV Sumber Rejeki", bought 500gr Gula Pasir for Rp15.000 fully on credit → journal posted debit Persediaan/credit Utang Dagang Rp15.000 correctly (2-line entry, no Kas & Bank line since paid_amount=0), stock updated 1000→1500gr. Paid Rp10.000 installment → journal posted debit Utang Dagang/credit Kas & Bank Rp10.000, purchase row updated to "Sisa Rp5.000", supplier badge showed "Utang Rp5.000", Neraca stayed balanced throughout (Aset = Kewajiban + Modal confirmed after each step).
- UI quirk hit during testing, useful for future preview-tool sessions on this project: clicking a `useActionState`-wired submit button (`<form action={formAction}>`, a React-specific mechanism) immediately after `window.location.href` navigation can silently no-op if it fires before hydration completes — no network request, no error, just nothing happens. Re-clicking (or waiting a beat) after confirming the click actually landed fixes it. This is distinct from the earlier-documented plain-`onClick`-button pattern (edit-ingredient-form.tsx-style inline forms), which doesn't have this hydration race since... actually both need hydration; the symptom just presents differently (edit forms fail to open at all if unhydrated, vs. server-action forms open fine but silently eat the submit).

name: mini-erp-scope
description: "Mini-ERP feature gap analysis against the \"Koenang Resto\" reference HTML the user shared, and what's been built so far"

  node_type: memory
  type: project

User wants KasirKu to grow toward a "mini ERP" (2026-07-08), modeled loosely on a reference prototype (`Koenang Resto` — a separate accounting + cost-control app, file at `D:\Users\ASTRI\Downloads\index.html`, an iframe shell only — actual module content in `modules/akuntansi.html`/`modules/costcontrol.html` was never shared). Explicit instruction: doesn't need to be complete, and must not disrupt the existing system — see [[project-purpose-saas-product]].

**Why:** the reference's sidebar reveals the target feature set even without the module internals: Akuntansi (COA/Jurnal/Neraca/Arus Kas/Target vs Aktual), Cost Control & HPP (kalkulator HPP, database bahan, cost control, laporan COGS, tren harga), Operasional (pembelian, stok, penjualan, invoice, kas harian, rekon rekening, supplier/hutang), SDM (absensi, payroll, lembur, THR, karyawan).

**Gap analysis against KasirKu's actual code (verified by reading source, not assumed):**
- Already covered, no rebuild needed: Laba Rugi (cash-basis, `reports/laba-rugi`), Payroll+Absensi, Kelola Produk/Bahan Baku, Riwayat Transaksi, Kelola Kasir.
- **Hitung HPP** — already exists: `products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` → `recalculateProductCost()` auto-recomputes `products.cost` from `product_recipes × ingredients.unit_cost` on every add/remove.
- **Cost Control (teori vs aktual)** — already exists in full inside `finance/page.tsx` (~line 187-256): COGS Teori (recipe-based) vs COGS Aktual (opening + pembelian − closing inventory), with a variance box and qualitative waste/efficiency notes. Not obvious from the nav alone — read the file before assuming this is missing.
- **Laporan COGS (per-produk/kategori breakdown)** — was genuinely missing; **built 2026-07-08** at `reports/cogs/page.tsx`, linked from the sidebar ("📐 Laporan COGS" in dashboard-shell.tsx) and cross-linked from `finance/page.tsx`'s Kontrol HPP section. diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index 53fcfdf..4323ea5 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -69,10 +69,4 @@ Mengikuti urutan modul di `docs/reference/skema-database-kasirku.md`:
 
 Setiap tabel dengan `business_id` diamankan dengan RLS lewat `private.owns_business(business_id)` — akses hanya untuk businesses milik `auth.uid()` yang sedang login. Tabel anak yang tidak punya `business_id` langsung (`product_recipes`, `transaction_items`, dll) diamankan lewat `EXISTS` join ke tabel induknya.
 
-## Keputusan desain yang masih perlu diambil
-
-Belum diimplementasikan di migration ini — perlu diputuskan sebelum modul terkait mulai di-porting:
-
-- **Verifikasi PIN kasir**: RLS `cashiers` saat ini hanya mengizinkan `owner_id = auth.uid()` (pemilik akun) membaca `pin_hash`. Karena kasir individual tidak punya akun Supabase Auth sendiri (hanya pemilik bisnis yang login), verifikasi PIN sebaiknya lewat Postgres function (`security definer` RPC) yang menerima `cashier_id` + PIN plaintext dan mengembalikan boolean — supaya `pin_hash` tidak perlu ter-expose ke client sama sekali.
-- **Self-order dari pelanggan (scan QR meja)**: pelanggan yang scan QR di meja tidak login sebagai pemilik bisnis, jadi policy `private.owns_business()` pada `self_orders`/`self_order_items` akan memblokir mereka melakukan INSERT. Perlu policy tambahan yang scoped ke `anon` role (misalnya izinkan INSERT kalau `table_id` valid & `self_orders.status = 'baru'`), atau proses lewat Edge Function dengan service role.
-- **Tutup shift**: kalkulasi `cash_sales`/`non_cash_sales`/`total_sales`/`expected_cash`/`difference` sebaiknya jadi Postgres function (RPC) supaya atomic, bukan dihitung di client lalu di-`UPDATE` — sesuai catatan di dokumen skema asli.
+Operasi yang butuh privilege di luar RLS pemilik bisnis (verifikasi PIN kasir, self-order pelanggan lewat scan QR, tutup shift) jalan lewat Postgres function `security definer`: `verify_cashier_pin`, `get_self_order_menu`/`submit_self_order`, dan `close_shift` — lihat masing-masing migration di `supabase/migrations/`.

You're auditing a Next.js + Supabase POS app (KasirKu) at G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu for correctness bugs in its financial calculations. This is a read-only investigation — do not edit any files, just report findings.

Focus area: checkout/transaction totals and payment reconciliation math. Specifically:

1. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/actions.ts` — find the checkout logic (likely calls a `checkout_transaction` RPC). Trace how subtotal, discount, PPN/tax, service charge, and final total are computed and passed to the RPC. Also check the change/kembalian calculation if cash payment.
2. Find the `checkout_transaction` RPC definition in `supabase/migrations/*.sql` (search for `create or replace function public.checkout_transaction` or similar — there may be multiple versions across migrations; the LATEST one wins, so identify the most recent redefinition and read that one closely). Verify: does discount apply before or after tax/service in the stored total? Is there any double-counting or rounding issue? Does it correctly write item-level `price`/`cost`/`qty` for COGS reporting to be accurate later?
3. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/pos/pos-screen.tsx` — find where discount/tax/service/total are calculated client-side for display before checkout. Compare this formula against what the RPC computes — do they match? A client/server mismatch would show the cashier one total but charge/record another.
4. Read the merchant-fee reconciliation table in `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/page.tsx` (search for "Rekonsiliasi Pembayaran" / "merchant_fees" / "fee_percent"). Verify the NET calculation (Total POS - fee%) is arithmetically correct, and that SELISIH (variance) = Aktual - Net is computed correctly, not backwards.

Report back: for each formula, quote the exact code (file:line) and state whether it's correct or describe the bug precisely (what inputs produce a wrong output, and why). Do NOT report style/architecture opinions — only correctness. If everything checks out, say so plainly per area. Keep the report under 600 words plus code quotes.

input.description: Audit HPP/COGS and weighted-average cost math
input.prompt:
You're auditing a Next.js + Supabase POS/mini-ERP app (KasirKu) at G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu for correctness bugs in its cost/HPP calculations. Read-only investigation — do not edit files, just report findings.

Focus area: product cost (HPP), recipe-based costing, and weighted-average inventory cost updates. Specifically:

1. Find and read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts` — the `recalculateProductCost()` function. Verify the formula: does it correctly sum `product_recipes.qty × ingredients.unit_cost` for all recipe lines of a product? Check unit conversion — if a recipe uses grams but the ingredient's `unit_cost` is per-kg (or similar mismatches), that would silently produce wrong costs. Does this function get called on every recipe add/remove/edit, or could it go stale?

2. Weighted-average cost recalculation appears in THREE places that each independently reimplement the same formula — find and compare all three, they must be identical or one is a latent bug:
   - `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/actions.ts` — `addExpense`, the ingredient-purchase branch (`isIngredientPurchase`)
   - `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/actions.ts` — `addExpense`, the product-purchase branch (`isProductPurchase`)
   - `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/purchases/actions.ts` — `addPurchase`, both the ingredient and product branches
   For each, the formula should be: `newUnitCost = round((oldStock × oldUnitCost + purchaseAmount) / newStock)`. Quote each implementation and check they match exactly (same rounding, same order of operations, no off-by-one on which stock value — old vs new — is used as the divisor).

3. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/reports/cogs/page.tsx` — verify `marginOf()` and `marginPctOf()`: margin = revenue - cogs, marginPct = margin/revenue × 100, rounded. Check there's no division-by-zero when revenue is 0 (should show "—" not crash/NaN).

4. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/page.tsx` — find the "Kontrol HPP — Teori vs Aktual" section. Verify: COGS Teori = sum of (item cost × qty) from sold items in the period. COGS Aktual = Persediaan Awal + Pembelian − Persediaan Akhir. Check the sign/direction is right (a common bug: swapping awal/akhir would invert the whole calculation).

Report back: for each formula, quote exact code (file:line) and state correct/bug with a concrete failing input if there's a bug. Skip style opinions. Under 700 words plus quotes.

input.description: Audit accounting module journal & balance math
input.prompt:
You're auditing a Next.js + Supabase mini-ERP accounting module (KasirKu) at G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu for correctness bugs in its double-entry bookkeeping calculations. Read-only investigation — do not edit files, just report findings.

Context: this module was built across several migrations this week: `supabase/migrations/20260708300000_accounting_core.sql`, `20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql`, `20260708300200_budgets.sql`, `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql`. Pages live under `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/accounting/` and `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/purchases/`.

Focus areas:

1. `private.post_journal()` in `20260708300000_accounting_core.sql` — verify the balance check sums all lines' debit and credit correctly and rejects unbalanced entries (`round(v_total_debit,2) <> round(v_total_credit,2)`). Any float/rounding edge case that could let a genuinely unbalanced entry slip through, or reject a balanced one due to rounding?

2. Read `20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql` — the sales-journal-posting logic added to `checkout_transaction`, and the reversing entry added to `void_transaction`. Verify: does the sales entry debit the correct payment-method-aware account (Kas & Bank vs Piutang for credit sales, if applicable), credit Pendapatan Penjualan for the right amount (before or after discount — should be net revenue), and does it correctly add HPP/Persediaan lines only when recipe cost data exists? Does the void's reversing entry use the EXACT SAME amounts as the original sale (not recomputed, which could drift if prices changed since)?

3. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/accounting/neraca/page.tsx` — verify Total Aset, Total Kewajiban, Total Modal sums are correct, and the "Laba Berjalan" (running profit) line correctly equals pendapatan-minus-beban-to-date from the journal (not from a different/stale source). Check the "seimbang" (balanced) check: does it actually compare Aset vs (Kewajiban + Modal), or could it silently show "balanced" when it isn't due to a bug in which accounts get bucketed into which section (check the account `type` → section mapping)?

4. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx` — verify the cash-flow bucketing (Operasional vs Investasi & Pendanaan) sums only journal lines touching the Kas & Bank account, and that debit-vs-credit sign convention correctly maps to cash-in vs cash-out.

5. Read `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/accounting/anggaran/page.tsx` — verify the actual-vs-target variance: for `pendapatan` accounts, actual should be credit-heavy so the code negates raw debit-minus-credit; for `beban` accounts it should NOT negate. ## Findings

**1. `recalculateProductCost()` formula — correct, but goes stale on the common path (STALENESS BUG)**

`src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts:8-20`
```ts
const totalCost = (items ?? []).reduce((sum, item) => {
  const ingredient = item.ingredients as unknown as { unit_cost: number } | null;
  return sum + Number(ingredient?.unit_cost ?? 0) * Number(item.qty);
}, 0);
await supabase.from("products").update({ cost: totalCost }).eq("id", productId);
```
The sum(qty × unit_cost) formula itself is correct, and unit conversion is not actually a bug here: `ingredients.unit` is a single field (e.g. "gr") that governs both stock and `unit_cost`, and `product_recipes.qty`/`unit` are copied from that same ingredient at insert time (`recipe/actions.ts:57`) with no separate purchase-unit vs recipe-unit concept — so there's no gram/kg mismatch possible in the schema as implemented.

The real bug: `recalculateProductCost` is only invoked from `addRecipeItem` (line 64) and `removeRecipeItem` (line 77) — i.e., only when a recipe *line* is added/removed. It is never called when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changes, which happens in three other places: `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient` (line 120), `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense` ingredient-purchase branch (line 104), and `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase` ingredient branch (line 105). None of these three call `recalculateProductCost` for the products that reference the ingredient. Concrete failure: a product's recipe uses flour at unit_cost=10000; product.cost is cached at e.g. 5000. A purchase raises flour's weighted-average unit_cost to 15000. `products.cost` still shows the stale 5000 until someone manually re-adds/removes a recipe line for that product. Since `transaction_items.cost` (used for COGS Teori in both the COGS report and finance page) is presumably snapshotted from `products.cost` at sale time, every sale in between records understated COGS/HPP.

**2. Weighted-average cost formula — all four call sites are identical (no bug)**

All four use `newUnitCost = round((oldStock×oldUnitCost + purchaseAmount) / newStock)`, guarding `newStock > 0`:
- `finance/actions.ts:97-100` (ingredient): `oldValue = stock*unit_cost; newStock = stock+qty; newUnitCost = newStock>0 ? Math.round((oldValue+amount)/newStock) : unit_cost;`
- `finance/actions.ts:141-143` (product): same pattern with `cost` instead of `unit_cost`.
- `purchases/actions.ts:98-101` (ingredient): identical to finance's ingredient branch.
- `purchases/actions.ts:137-139` (product): identical to finance's product branch.

All four use `newStock` (old+qty) as divisor and `oldValue+amount` as numerator — correct direction, consistent rounding (`Math.round`), consistent order of operations. No discrepancy found.

**3. `reports/cogs/page.tsx` — correct**

`marginOf` (line 28-30): `row.revenue - row.cogs` — correct.
`marginPctOf` (line 32-34): `row.revenue > 0 ? Math.round((marginOf(row) / row.revenue) * 100) : null` — correctly guards divide-by-zero; UI renders `"—"` when null (lines 213, 260, 310). No bug.

**4. `finance/page.tsx` — "Kontrol HPP — Teori vs Aktual" — correct direction**

`cogsAktual = openingValue + totalPembelian - closingValue` (line 231) matches the spec Persediaan Awal + Pembelian − Persediaan Akhir; not swapped. `selisih = cogsAktual - cogsTeori` (line 234) and `selisihPct` guards `cogsTeori > 0` (line 235). `cogsTeori` is summed from `transactions.total_cost` (line 108), which inherits the staleness described in finding 1 if `products.cost` was stale when the sale was recorded — this is a downstream symptom, not a separate bug in this file.

## Summary of Findings

**1. `private.post_journal()` balance check — correct, no bug.**
`supabase/migrations/20260708300000_accounting_core.sql:158-176`. `v_total_debit`/`v_total_credit` are typed `numeric(14,2)`, so each accumulation is already rounded to 2dp; the trailing `round(...,2)` is redundant but harmless. Any line violating one-sidedness fails the `journal_lines_one_sided` check constraint at insert and aborts the whole transaction (not silently absorbed into a "balanced" total). No float/rounding edge case found.

**2. Checkout/void posting — mostly correct, two real gaps.**
`checkout_transaction` (`20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql:246-260`) debits `1-001` and credits `4-001` for `v_total`, which is computed from `v_subtotal = v_subtotal_raw - v_total_item_disc - v_order_disc_amt` (line 204) — net-of-discount, correct. There is no credit-sale/Piutang payment method in the app (payment methods are just labels via `custom_payment_methods`), so always debiting Kas & Bank is correct, not a bug.
Gap found: the journal is only posted `if v_total > 0` (line 246), but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally (lines 173-192). A 100%-discounted item (`v_disc_type='pct', v_disc=100`, or `p_order_disc=100`) reduces inventory/ingredient stock with **no HPP/Persediaan journal entry at all**, even when `v_total_cost > 0` — COGS silently disappears for fully-discounted sales.
`void_transaction` (lines 345-359) correctly reuses `v_tx.total`/`v_tx.total_cost` read back from the `transactions` row (captured at original checkout), not recomputed — no price-drift risk. Correct.

**3. Neraca (`neraca/page.tsx`) — arithmetic is correct by construction, but the "seimbang" check can mask upstream failures.**
`balanceOf()` (lines 64-67) uses each account's own `normal_balance`, and `daftar-akun/actions.ts:29` always derives `normal_balance` from `type` deterministically (`type === "aset" || type === "beban" ? "debit" : "kredit"`), so type↔normal_balance is never mismatched — the section bucketing is safe. `selisih = totalAset - (totalKewajiban + totalModal)` where `totalModal = totalModalRecorded + labaBerjalan` (lines 80-82) is mathematically guaranteed to be 0 whenever every posted entry is balanced (standard trial-balance identity), so "seimbang" is a legitimate check, not a fake one.
However, real bug elsewhere feeds this: several journal-posting call sites never check the RPC's error result, so a failed post (e.g. renamed/missing account code) silently leaves the purchase/expense recorded in its own table but **absent from the journal** — Neraca will still report "✓ seimbang" while Persediaan/Kas/Utang are understated for that transaction:
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/purchases/actions.ts:27` (`await supabase.rpc("post_journal_entry", ...)`, no `{ error }` check) and line 246 (same, in `addPurchasePayment`)
- `src/app/business/[businessId]/(dashboard)/finance/actions.ts:33` (`postExpenseJournal`, same pattern)
Contrast with `accounting/jurnal/actions.ts:51-60`, which does check `error`. This is a genuine correctness gap: the balance sheet's "balanced" indicator gives false confidence when postings silently fail.

**4. Arus Kas (`arus-kas/page.tsx`) — sign convention is correct; bucketing has a real bug.**
`masuk += debit; keluar += credit` for lines on the Kas & Bank account (lines 94-98) is correct (Kas is debit-normal, so a debit = cash in). But:
```
const OPERASIONAL_SOURCES = new Set(["penjualan", "void", "pembelian", "beban", "payroll"]); // line 14
```
`public.post_journal_entry` (`20260708300000_accounting_core.sql:227-229`) hardcodes `source := 'manual'` for every call, and it is the **only** RPC used by `purchases/actions.ts` (both `addPurchase`'s inventory purchase and `addPurchasePayment`) and by `finance/actions.ts`'s `postExpenseJournal` ("Catat Pengeluaran"). No code path ever posts with `source='pembelian'`, `'beban'`, or `'payroll'` — only `checkout_transaction`/`void_transaction` call `private.post_journal` directly with real sources. Result: every purchase and every recorded expense is bucketed into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Aktivitas Operasional", while `SOURCE_LABELS` for `pembelian`/`beban`/`payroll` (lines 16-23) are dead code. This materially misclassifies the cash-flow statement.

**5. Anggaran (`anggaran/page.tsx`) — correct.**
```
const actual = a.type === "pendapatan" ? -rawActual : rawActual;   // line 83
const pct = target > 0 ? Math.round((actual / target) * 100) : null; // line 85
```
`rawActual = Σ(debit - credit)`; negating for `pendapatan` (credit-normal) and leaving `beban` (debit-normal) as-is is correct, and `pct` guards against division by zero, rendering "—" instead of crashing.

**6. `purchases/actions.ts` — correct.**
`postPurchaseJournal` (lines 17-26): debit `1-200` for full `amount`, credit `1-001` for `paidAmount`, credit `2-001` for `amount - paidAmount` — always balances since `sisaUtang := amount - paidAmount` by construction, and `paidAmount > amount` is rejected client-side (line 66-68) and by the DB check `purchases_paid_not_over_amount` (`20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql:40`). `addPurchasePayment` (lines 218-221) correctly rejects `amount > sisaUtang`. Only issue is the unguarded RPC error noted in (3)/(4) above.

**How to apply:** before building anything else from this reference, grep/read the relevant existing page first — this module has repeatedly turned out to already cover more than the sidebar-only feature list suggested. As of 2026-07-09 every item originally identified in this gap analysis has been built and verified E2E — no queued next candidate remains; ask the user what's next if resuming this thread.

**Formula audit — 2026-07-09**, after all the above was built, ran 4 parallel Explore agents auditing every calculation in the app (POS checkout/merchant-fee, HPP/COGS/weighted-avg cost, accounting/journal/balance-sheet, payroll/shift-close/ticket-pricing). Most formulas checked out clean (checkout math, weighted-average cost, Neraca arithmetic, Anggaran variance, payroll, shift-close, ticket pricing — the last one has existing passing unit tests, 38/38). **4 real bugs found, 1 fixed so far:**
1. **FIXED (commit bdbe337)**: Arus Kas (`accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`) bucketed cash flow by `journal_entries.source`, but `public.post_journal_entry` (used by every purchase and expense posting, not just true manual entries) always writes `source='manual'` — so nearly all purchases/expenses were misclassified into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Operasional". Fixed by classifying by the counterparty account's type/code instead (modal→Pendanaan, Peralatan 1-500→Investasi, else→Operasional). Verified in browser: Beban Lain-lain, Bayar Utang Dagang, and a cash Persediaan purchase all correctly moved to "Aktivitas Operasional".
2. **NOT YET FIXED**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only re-fires on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changes via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`. So `products.cost` (and therefore `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time, and therefore COGS Teori in both the COGS report and finance page's Kontrol HPP) silently goes stale whenever an ingredient's price changes without someone re-touching that product's recipe.
3. **NOT YET FIXED (minor/edge case)**: `checkout_transaction` (`20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql`) only posts a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduces inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all, so COGS silently disappears from the books for that sale.
4. **NOT YET FIXED (silent-failure risk)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` call the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }` (unlike `accounting/jurnal/actions.ts`, which does check). If a posting ever fails (e.g. a renamed/missing account code), the purchase/expense row still saves but the journal entry silently doesn't exist — Neraca would still show "✓ seimbang" while understating the real numbers for that transaction.
See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.

**Supplier & Hutang (formal Pembelian) — built and verified E2E 2026-07-09**: migration `20260709110000_suppliers_purchases.sql` (see [[supabase-migrations-manual]]) adds `public.suppliers` (name/phone/address/notes, soft-delete), `public.purchases` (supplier_id nullable, category constrained to `'Bahan Baku'|'Barang Dagang'`, optional ingredient_id/product_id + qty, amount, paid_amount with a `paid_amount <= amount` check), and `public.purchase_payments` (installment log). lines: **Formula audit — 2026-07-09**, after all the above was built, ran 4 parallel Explore agents auditing every calculation in the app (POS checkout/merchant-fee, HPP/COGS/weighted-avg cost, accounting/journal/balance-sheet, payroll/shift-close/ticket-pricing). Most formulas checked out clean (checkout math, weighted-average cost, Neraca arithmetic, Anggaran variance, payroll, shift-close, ticket pricing — the last one has existing passing unit tests, 38/38). **4 real bugs found, 1 fixed so far:**

1. **FIXED (commit bdbe337)**: Arus Kas (`accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`) bucketed cash flow by `journal_entries.source`, but `public.post_journal_entry` (used by every purchase and expense posting, not just true manual entries) always writes `source='manual'` — so nearly all purchases/expenses were misclassified into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Operasional". Fixed by classifying by the counterparty account's type/code instead (modal→Pendanaan, Peralatan 1-500→Investasi, else→Operasional). Verified in browser: Beban Lain-lain, Bayar Utang Dagang, and a cash Persediaan purchase all correctly moved to "Aktivitas Operasional".

-2. **NOT YET FIXED**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only re-fires on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changes via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`. So `products.cost` (and therefore `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time, and therefore COGS Teori in both the COGS report and finance page's Kontrol HPP) silently goes stale whenever an ingredient's price changes without someone re-touching that product's recipe.

+2. **FIXED (commit b928d51)**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only used to re-fire on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changed via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`, so `products.cost` (and downstream, `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time → COGS Teori) silently went stale. Fixed by extracting the calc into `src/lib/recalculate-product-cost.ts` (`recalculateProductCost` + a new `recalculateProductCostsForIngredient` that finds every product referencing a given ingredient and recalcs each) and calling the ingredient-scoped version from all three write sites whenever `unit_cost` actually changes. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": added Gula Pasir (50gr) to Roti Bakar's recipe (HPP → Rp1.350 at Rp27/gr), then edited Gula Pasir's price to Rp100/gr manually — Roti Bakar's HPP updated to Rp5.000 without touching the recipe. Then bought 100gr more via the Pembelian page (weighted avg → Rp106/gr) — HPP updated again to Rp5.300, confirming all three trigger paths work.

3. **NOT YET FIXED (minor/edge case)**: `checkout_transaction` (`20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql`) only posts a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduces inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all, so COGS silently disappears from the books for that sale.

4. **NOT YET FIXED (silent-failure risk)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` call the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }` (unlike `accounting/jurnal/actions.ts`, which does check). If a posting ever fails (e.g. a renamed/missing account code), the purchase/expense row still saves but the journal entry silently doesn't exist — Neraca would still show "✓ seimbang" while understating the real numbers for that transaction.
See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.

input.command:
cd "G:\PROJECT1\KasirKu" && git add supabase/migrations/20260709120000_fix_zero_total_hpp_posting.sql && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix HPP/Persediaan journal lines missing on 100%-discounted sales

checkout_transaction only posted a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but
stock/ingredient consumption happens regardless of discount — so a
100%-discounted sale (v_total = 0, v_total_cost > 0) silently recorded
no HPP/Persediaan entry at all, understating COGS. Decoupled the
Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines (only when there's revenue) from the
HPP/Persediaan lines (independently, whenever there's cost), mirrored
in void_transaction's reversing entry. Verified in browser: a 100%-off
Roti Bakar sale (INV-20260709-0001) now posts a 2-line entry debiting
HPP/crediting Persediaan Rp5.300 with no revenue lines.
EOF
)"

lines: **Formula audit — 2026-07-09**, after all the above was built, ran 4 parallel Explore agents auditing every calculation in the app (POS checkout/merchant-fee, HPP/COGS/weighted-avg cost, accounting/journal/balance-sheet, payroll/shift-close/ticket-pricing). Most formulas checked out clean (checkout math, weighted-average cost, Neraca arithmetic, Anggaran variance, payroll, shift-close, ticket pricing — the last one has existing passing unit tests, 38/38). **4 real bugs found, 1 fixed so far:**

1. **FIXED (commit bdbe337)**: Arus Kas (`accounting/arus-kas/page.tsx`) bucketed cash flow by `journal_entries.source`, but `public.post_journal_entry` (used by every purchase and expense posting, not just true manual entries) always writes `source='manual'` — so nearly all purchases/expenses were misclassified into "Investasi & Pendanaan" instead of "Operasional". Fixed by classifying by the counterparty account's type/code instead (modal→Pendanaan, Peralatan 1-500→Investasi, else→Operasional). Verified in browser: Beban Lain-lain, Bayar Utang Dagang, and a cash Persediaan purchase all correctly moved to "Aktivitas Operasional".

2. **FIXED (commit b928d51)**: `recalculateProductCost()` (`products/[productId]/recipe/actions.ts`) only used to re-fire on recipe line add/remove — never when an ingredient's `unit_cost` changed via `ingredients/actions.ts` `editIngredient`, `finance/actions.ts` `addExpense`, or `purchases/actions.ts` `addPurchase`, so `products.cost` (and downstream, `transaction_items.cost` snapshotted at sale time → COGS Teori) silently went stale. Fixed by extracting the calc into `src/lib/recalculate-product-cost.ts` (`recalculateProductCost` + a new `recalculateProductCostsForIngredient` that finds every product referencing a given ingredient and recalcs each) and calling the ingredient-scoped version from all three write sites whenever `unit_cost` actually changes. Verified in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": added Gula Pasir (50gr) to Roti Bakar's recipe (HPP → Rp1.350 at Rp27/gr), then edited Gula Pasir's price to Rp100/gr manually — Roti Bakar's HPP updated to Rp5.000 without touching the recipe. Then bought 100gr more via the Pembelian page (weighted avg → Rp106/gr) — HPP updated again to Rp5.300, confirming all three trigger paths work.

-3. **NOT YET FIXED (minor/edge case)**: `checkout_transaction` (`20260708300100_checkout_void_journal_posting.sql`) only posts a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduces inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all, so COGS silently disappears from the books for that sale.

+3. **FIXED (commit e02e62d, migration `20260709120000_fix_zero_total_hpp_posting.sql`)**: `checkout_transaction` only posted a journal entry `if v_total > 0`, but stock/ingredient consumption happens unconditionally — a 100%-discounted sale reduced inventory with no HPP/Persediaan journal line at all. Fixed by decoupling the Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines (posted only when `v_total > 0`) from the HPP/Persediaan lines (posted independently whenever `v_total_cost > 0`), building `v_journal_lines` incrementally and only calling `private.post_journal` if at least 2 lines ended up in it. Mirrored the identical fix in `void_transaction`'s reversing entry. Verified end-to-end in browser on "Toko Test Laporan": sold 1 Roti Bakar (HPP Rp5.300) with a 100% order discount (INV-20260709-0001, total Rp0) — jurnal correctly posted a 2-line entry (debit 5-001 HPP / credit 1-200 Persediaan, Rp5.300, no Kas & Bank/Pendapatan lines). Then voided it with manager PIN — reversing entry correctly posted debit 1-200 / credit 5-001, Rp5.300. Neraca stayed balanced throughout.

4. **NOT YET FIXED (silent-failure risk)**: `purchases/actions.ts` and `finance/actions.ts` call the `post_journal_entry` RPC via `supabase.rpc(...)` without checking `{ error }` (unlike `accounting/jurnal/actions.ts`, which does check). If a posting ever fails (e.g. a renamed/missing account code), the purchase/expense row still saves but the journal entry silently doesn't exist — Neraca would still show "✓ seimbang" while understating the real numbers for that transaction.
See [[supabase-migrations-manual]] if any future fix here needs a new migration.

Now `postExpenseJournal`/`postPurchaseJournal` return the error message (or null) instead of swallowing it, and both call sites plus the utang-payment RPC call in `addPurchasePayment` check it: on failure they log a `"warning"` activity entry (instead of the usual success level) with the error text, and return a form error telling the user the record saved but a manual correcting journal entry is needed at Akuntansi → Jurnal.
